nodes.name: Ni-Fe PBA Nanocubes Complete Synthesis
nodes.procedure: In a typical synthesis procedure, 698 mg of nickel (II) nitrate hexahydrate and 882 mg of sodium citrate tribasic dihydrate were fully dissolved in 80 ml of deionized water using sonication, forming solution A. Meanwhile, 528 mg of potassium hexacyanoferrate (III) was dissolved in 120 ml of deionized water to prepare solution B. Solution B was then swiftly combined with solution A in 15 s under magnetic stirring, followed by 1 min of additional stirring. The mixture was left to stand at room temperature for 24 hours. The resulting yellow precipitate was harvested through repeated cycles of centrifugation and washing with deionized water and ethanol. Finally, the products were dried overnight in a vacuum oven at 70°C.

nodes.name: Ni-Fe PBA Nanocages by Acid Etching
nodes.procedure: To synthesize the Ni-Fe PBA nanocages, an acid etching method assisted by tannic acid (TA) was utilized. Initially, 20 mg of as-synthesized Ni-Fe PBA nanocubes and 1200 mg of TA were thoroughly dissolved in 40 ml of isopropanol assisted by sonication. Subsequently, 10 ml of a 1 M hydrochloric acid solution was added to this mixture. The resulting solution was then transferred to a Teflon-lined stainless-steel autoclave and heated at 140°C for 6 hours. The product was obtained through multiple cycles of centrifugation and washing with ethanol, followed by overnight drying in a vacuum oven at 70°C.

nodes.name: Ni-Fe-P Nanocages Phosphatization
nodes.procedure: The thermochemical treatment method was used to convert Ni-Fe PBA nanocages to Ni-Fe-P nanocages. Briefly, 20 mg of Ni-Fe PBA nanocages and 200 mg of NaH2PO2 powder were placed in two separate porcelain boats within a tube furnace, with the nanocages positioned downstream and the NaH2PO2 powder upstream. The samples were heated at 350°C for 1 to 2 hours at a rate of 5°C per minute under a nitrogen atmosphere. After the treatment, the samples were allowed to cool to room temperature while still under nitrogen protection before being collected.

nodes.description: OER performance evaluation in 1.0 M KOH using three-electrode setup

catalyst_ink.value: 3 mg catalyst + 0.3 ml water + 0.288 ml isopropanol + 0.012 ml 5 wt% Nafion (50 µl drop cast)

nodes.source_text: The evaluation of the electrocatalytic performance... was conducted in a standard three-electrode setup... in a 1.0 M KOH electrolyte (pH 13.80±0.01)... Catalyst ink (50 µl) was drop cast on carbon fiber paper... (1 mg cm⁻²)... Consecutive CV curves... low overpotentials of 221, 264, and 297 mV to achieve current densities of 10, 50, and 100 mA cm⁻²... remarkable electrocatalytic stability... after over 100 hours of chronopotentiometric testing at 50 and 100 mA cm⁻².

nodes.description: Operando CV-XAFS for OER structural evolution (slow scan)

stages.value: resting (0.9-1.2 V), pre-catalytic (1.2-1.4 V), catalytic (1.4-1.9 V)

nodes.source_text: CV-XAFS experiments, a slow scan rate of 1 mV s⁻¹... structure S_III... approximately 15% of the Fe-P local structure is converted to Fe-O... second CV scan... Fe-O coordination percentage increases to about 20%... only a small portion of the Ni-P bonds (about 10%)... long-term reaction-conditioned Ni-Fe-P catalyst... complete conversion of Fe-P to Fe-O, accompanied by only ∼40% conversion of Ni-P to Ni-O.

nodes.description: Operando CA-XAFS for OER structural evolution at fixed potentials
nodes.source_text: operando CA-XAFS experiments... at applied potentials of 0.9 V, 1.5 V, and 1.9 V... Fe-O coordination percentage... up to 20% at 1.9 V... Ni-O coordination... only 10% at 1.9 V... Fe-P bond... undergoes gradual elongation... Debye-Waller factor for the Fe-P path... 0.003 Å²... rising to 0.010 Å² at 1.9 V.

S7; and table S1).
